name: Rocket Man #9
description:
Little Rocket Man: The Rough Beginning by Mad Monk

26 artworks and a sound track on Async Art Blueprints

...

I had started working on the Little Rocket Man angle earlier during the summer of 2022. Using the AI text to image I built up the first images but decided to shelf the project until it matured more in my mind. I took it up again during October to finalize the images. Having seen the capability of Async Art Music, I decided add a chaotic disturbing soundtrack to go along with the images. The 26 images here are mostly v1 or say the rough images from the project. They are gritty and confusing - much aligned with the subject matter. I plan to release the v2s which are are cleaner versions that follow and build on this first set. 

The soundtrack to go along with the project is a work by Hulki Okan Tabak who loves to play with loops and went to build the right fit with the idea of a chaotic disturbing sound scheme.

26 artworks are all 1/1s from the same project file and the soundtrack is reproduced alongside each one of them.

...

"According to The Chosun IIbo, a South Korean newspaper, Trump and Kim discussed “Rocket Man” during a lunch between the two in Singapore last month. Kim mentioned that Trump had referred to him as “Rocket Man” last year when North Korea was engaging in nuclear tests and missile launches.

The source with knowledge of the talks told CNN that Trump asked whether Kim knew where he’d gotten the nickname, and Kim said no. Trump asked Kim if he had heard of the Elton John song. Kim replied no, and that he had never heard of John. Trump told Kim that John is really good and that he would send him the song. The source added that Trump asked Kim if he minded being called “Rocket Man,” and Kim said no.

Trump had started calling Kim “Little Rocket Man” or simply “Rocket Man” last year as an insult. However, Trump has recently been criticized for his praise of the North Korean dictator, calling him “honorable” and touting their chemistry." --- excerpt from CNN web site, 2018
